drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that the firstborn is eaten for two days and a night?
outcomeNote: Firstborn's eating time derived by hekesh to peace offerings; the baraita continues in the next unit.

segments.he: הַבְּכוֹר נֶאֱכָל לַכֹּהֲנִים. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן לַבְּכוֹר שֶׁנֶּאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין״ – הִקִּישׁוֹ הַכָּתוּב לְחָזֶה וָשׁוֹק שֶׁל שְׁלָמִים; מָה שְׁלָמִים נֶאֱכָלִין לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד, אַף בְּכוֹר נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «The firstborn» offering is «eaten by the priests,» throughout the city of Jerusalem, prepared in any manner of food preparation, for two days and one night. «The Sages taught» in a baraita: «From where» is it derived «with regard to a firstborn» offering «that» it is «eaten for two days and» the intervening «night?» It is derived from a verse, «as it is stated» with regard to a firstborn offering: «“And their flesh shall be yours, as the breast of waving and as the right thigh”» (Numbers 18:18). «The verse juxtaposes» the firstborn offering «with the breast and thigh of peace offerings. Just as peace offerings are eaten for two days and one night, so too, a firstborn» offering is «eaten for two days and one night.»
